svg.aria-label: Two ways to let a model act on a computer. On the left, a language model is given a goal and emits a string describing an action, which your code must parse and then trust, because the string can name a button, a path or a URL that does not exist. On the right, a System One model is given the list of controls that actually exist on screen, returns one typed choice from that list together with a calibrated probability, and your code executes it and independently verifies the outcome. The caption says the answer space is the list, so an action that is not on the list cannot be returned, which is a property of the interface rather than a promise about behaviour.
svg.text: THE MODEL PICKS. IT DOES NOT AUTHOR.
